facts.label: Analysis by dimension
facts.text: Leverage has climbed in each period on every EBITDA measure, and the climb is debt-driven. Gross debt at carrying value moved from 1.84x EBITDA in fiscal 2024 to 2.02x in fiscal 2025 and 2.29x on the last twelve months to 2026-06-30, and net debt from 1.55x to 1.68x to 2.21x. Reported EBITDA grew over the same span, so the rise comes from borrowing: the nine months to 2026-06-30 drew USD 302.74 million more than they repaid and the Term Loan B was enlarged on 2026-05-27, while buybacks and a receivables build absorbed cash. Creditors hold a larger claim on a business whose cash conversion is, for now, depressed. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Revenue is government-funded, concentrated and mostly performance-based, so transaction volumes, not price, decide earnings. The ten largest contracts gave about 60% of fiscal 2025 revenue, one federal agency about one-fifth of it, and performance-based contracts 54.4% of it; the effect is already visible in fiscal 2026, when U.S. Federal Services revenue fell 2.5% over nine months on lower volumes on large transaction-based contracts and less disaster-recovery work, while its operating margin rose to 17.5%. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses

facts.text: Cash conversion is average in a normal year and weak in the latest nine months. facts.text: Competition is credit-neutral to mildly negative. Competitors named in the annual report are large federal contractors and consultancies, buyer power is high because government customers rebid and can cancel for convenience, supplier power sits in labor, and the government may perform work itself, so pricing power is limited and margin gains come from efficiency, not price. facts.label: Competition and policy
facts.text: Policy is the largest outside influence. The 2025 federal statute adds Medicaid redeterminations every six months and work requirements from 2026-12-31 that states may delay, and ties SNAP funding to error rates from fiscal 2028; interest rates matter because part of the debt floats. These factors can raise demand for eligibility work or delay it, and federal budget or contract changes can cut revenue quickly, so they are credit-material and are carried into the monitoring triggers. Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36

facts.text: Over twelve to twenty-four months the guided fiscal 2026 outcome is revenue of USD 5.2 billion to USD 5.35 billion toward the lower end, adjusted EBITDA margin of about 13.7% and free cash flow of USD 425 million to USD 475 million, all lowered or held after the customer modification; the modification runs to 2026-12-31 and reduces diluted earnings per share by about USD 0.35 per quarter, roughly USD 18.57 million of net income a quarter on about 53.057 million diluted shares. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside is a federal payment delay that lasts longer than management expects, combined with a curtailed large contract. The first operational break is a receivable build that turns operating cash flow negative again, as it did in the nine months to 2026-06-30; cash, which was USD 56.953 million, is then replenished from the revolver (stated access about USD 730.0 million), from receivable sales (limit USD 350.0 million) or from new debt, and if the revolver were fully drawn carrying-value debt would reach 3.31x last-twelve-month EBITDA, an arithmetic bound that is not a covenant measure. Management's levers are slowing buybacks, trimming the dividend and capital spending, and the revolver; the resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 on the stated facilities, subject to terms of the credit agreement that were not supplied, and the observable triggers are days sales outstanding above 98 days, revolver drawings, a lower guidance range and further repurchases. Basis: calculation N6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 31–32; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1)

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Maximus presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, contract life and a government customer base, but credit quality is constrained by rising debt, weak recent cash conversion and shareholder returns that continued while cash was thin. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because fiscal 2025 free cash flow was strong and the delayed receipts are being collected, but the recovery is not yet shown in a balance sheet. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage and collections in 2029 and 2031. The primary downside path is a prolonged federal payment delay or a lost large contract while shareholder returns continue. Further analysis would require the results after 2026-06-30, the credit agreement and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: federal collections. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases support the requested credit work only to the quarter ended 2026-06-30, so every balance sheet and leverage figure creditors see is 128 days old at the 2026-11-05 as-of date.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C1

Nothing supplied covers the year ended 2026-09-30, the credit agreement and its May 2026 amendment, the proxy statement that holds governance detail, or any rating or market price. Management states that USD 245 million of delayed federal collections arrived after the quarter end, but no supplied balance sheet shows it.

## Request

MAXIMUS, INC. (mms), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot: the financial foundation (statements, constructed periods, leverage, interest cover, liquidity, debt and definition conflicts) built from the seven supplied SEC filings and earnings releases. The latest balance sheet is 2026-06-30 and the statements are in USD thousands.

## Findings
### Bottom line
Net debt rose to 2.21x last-twelve-month EBITDA at 2026-06-30 from 1.68x at 2025-09-30, while cash interest cover held at 8.28x, so leverage has increased without yet straining coverage.
Basis: calculation K21; calculation K22

The increase is financed by debt rather than earnings: the term loans were enlarged to fund operations and share repurchases while a federal customer paid late, so nine-month operating cash flow was negative. Management reports USD 245 million collected after the quarter end, which would lower net leverage to 1.87x on a pro forma basis, but the collection date and other post-quarter cash movements are not stated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation K17; calculation K18
Covenant headroom is not assessed because the credit agreement was not supplied; the company reports 2.00x against a maximum of 4.00x on its own definition, which differs from the measures used here.
### Analysis by dimension

Leverage has climbed in each period on every EBITDA measure, and the climb is debt-driven. Gross debt at carrying value moved from 1.84x EBITDA in fiscal 2024 to 2.02x in fiscal 2025 and 2.29x on the last twelve months to 2026-06-30, and net debt from 1.55x to 1.68x to 2.21x. Reported EBITDA grew over the same span, so the rise comes from borrowing: the nine months to 2026-06-30 drew USD 302.74 million more than they repaid and the Term Loan B was enlarged on 2026-05-27, while buybacks and a receivables build absorbed cash. Creditors hold a larger claim on a business whose cash conversion is, for now, depressed.

Basis: calculation K13; calculation K14; calculation K15; calculation K21; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30

Interest cover is strong and slightly improving, because EBITDA growth outpaced the cost of a larger, partly hedged floating-rate debt stack. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 7.78x in fiscal 2024, 8.02x in fiscal 2025 and 8.28x over the last twelve months, while swaps fix the rate on USD 675.0 million of the loans, roughly two-fifths of principal. The cushion is wide against the 3.00x minimum in the credit agreement as the company describes it, but that test uses a different EBITDA and interest definition, so no headroom is inferred.
Basis: calculation K21; calculation K24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32

Cash-flow quality is the weak point. Operating cash flow was negative in the nine months to 2026-06-30, USD -179.863 million against USD -220.000 million a year earlier, because the cash flow statement shows a receivables build of USD 489.403 million while a large federal customer delayed payment; days sales outstanding reached 98 days against 62 days at 2025-09-30, or 123 days against 73 days before the effect of receivable sales. Free cash flow was negative for the period. Fiscal 2025 operating cash flow of USD 429.372 million and free cash flow of USD 366.159 million show what the business generates when collections are normal, and management guides to a recovery by year end, so the credit question is the timing of one federal contract's payments rather than earnings power.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 51; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation K10; calculation K12

A receivables purchase programme with Wells Fargo acts as off-balance-sheet working-capital funding. Receivables of USD 1.28 billion were sold in the nine months to 2026-06-30 against USD 574.2 million a year earlier, with a facility limit that rose from USD 250.0 million to USD 350.0 million between the first and second quarters; the outstanding balance of sold receivables at each balance-sheet date is not stated. The programme lowers reported debt and receivables, so leverage on balance-sheet debt understates the funding the business relies on, and the facility would have to be replaced if it were withdrawn.

Liquidity is thin on cash and relies on committed lines. Unrestricted cash fell to USD 56.953 million at 2026-06-30 from USD 222.351 million at 2025-09-30, restricted cash of USD 96.296 million held for customers and as collateral is excluded from it, and the revolver gives stated access of about USD 730.0 million with USD 20.0 million drawn. Against gross debt at carrying value of USD 1,636.935 million, near-term liquidity therefore depends on the revolver, the receivables programme and the delayed collections; no letter-of-credit amount is stated after 2025-09-30, so whether the stated access is net of letters of credit is not established.

Claims outside the debt figure are modest but not nil. Operating lease liabilities of USD 94.883 million at 2026-06-30 are reported on their own lines and excluded from Total Debt; deferred compensation plan liabilities of USD 66.468 million are matched by plan assets of USD 67.877 million; performance bond commitments were USD 33.2 million at 2025-09-30 with no later figure stated; and the class actions arising from the 2023 MOVEit cybersecurity incident are accrued within a range of outcomes whose amount is not stated. The receivables purchase programme described above is the largest funding item outside debt.
Basis: calculation K27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 98

Maturities are manageable but cluster in fiscal 2029, when USD 690.184 million falls due, and the rest falls due by fiscal 2031 when the credit agreement ends; scheduled principal payments through September 2028 total USD 176.195 million, about a tenth of principal. Seven interest rate swaps hedge USD 675.0 million of the term loans, the earliest expiring in September 2026.
Basis: calculation K24; calculation K25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32

Three EBITDA measures coexist and the leverage ratios are not comparable across them. The credit agreement's Consolidated EBITDA is USD 798.419 million for the last twelve months, the company's adjusted measure is USD 711.009 million and reported EBITDA derived here is USD 714.036 million; the company's own net leverage of 2.00x nets only unrestricted cash and uses the credit-agreement measure, against 2.21x here. The figures used for ratios are the reported, carrying-value ones, with the adjusted twin shown beside them in the register; the difference between carrying value and principal debt is USD 16.613 million.
Basis: calculation K5; calculation K6; calculation K16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15

Events after the balance-sheet date are kept out of the period figures: the collection of USD 245 million, a quarterly dividend of USD 0.33 per share declared on 2026-07-06 and payable on 2026-08-31, a cash payment of about USD 17.3 million, and a temporary customer contract modification effective 2026-07-01 that management expects to cut diluted earnings per share by about USD 0.35 per quarter. The collection lowers net debt but its date and the offsetting cash uses are not stated, so the pro forma figure is indicative only.

Basis: calculation K17; calculation K26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4

The most material gaps are the absence of any figure after 2026-06-30, so the fiscal year-end balance sheet is unknown, and the absence of the credit agreement, which leaves covenant headroom, legal rank and instrument-level terms unstated. Each is logged under Gaps with its consequence.

## Findings
### Bottom line
Creditors rely on a large, long-dated government contract book whose main risks are concentration and collection timing rather than ownership, since no sponsor appears in the supplied documents.

Backlog of USD 15,327 million at 2025-09-30 had a weighted remaining life of 5.0 years, yet the ten largest contracts produced about 60% of fiscal 2025 revenue and almost all contracts can be cancelled for convenience, so one contract change moves earnings: a temporary modification on a major federal program cuts diluted earnings per share by about USD 0.35 per quarter. Management has kept returning cash to shareholders while borrowing, which makes capital allocation the governance point to monitor.
### Key findings

Revenue is government-funded, concentrated and mostly performance-based, so transaction volumes, not price, decide earnings. The ten largest contracts gave about 60% of fiscal 2025 revenue, one federal agency about one-fifth of it, and performance-based contracts 54.4% of it; the effect is already visible in fiscal 2026, when U.S. Federal Services revenue fell 2.5% over nine months on lower volumes on large transaction-based contracts and less disaster-recovery work, while its operating margin rose to 17.5%.

Contract life gives visibility but little protection. Backlog was USD 15,327 million with a weighted remaining life of 5.0 years, but almost all government contracts allow the customer to terminate or modify them at any time and pay only for work already done, so backlog is an estimate of potential revenue, not committed cash.

A single customer event reached earnings and cash in the same quarter. A major federal customer imposed a temporary modification from 2026-07-01 to 2026-12-31 that management expects to cut diluted earnings per share by about USD 0.35 per quarter, and payments on one large federal contract were delayed so that days sales outstanding reached 98 days; management reports USD 245 million collected after the quarter end and expects the days figure to finish the year below 70 days. For creditors the question is how quickly the receivable converts, because buybacks and dividends are paid from the same cash.

Demand drivers are supportive but depend on policy timing. Federal legislation signed in 2025 requires more frequent Medicaid redeterminations and work requirements for the expansion population from 2026-12-31, which states can ask to delay by up to two years, and management reports year-to-date signed awards of USD 1.25 billion against a sales pipeline of USD 50.4 billion; the U.S. Services segment, where revenue fell 6.4% over nine months, has to return to growth for that demand to reach earnings.

Capital allocation is the governance issue creditors should watch. Share repurchases were USD 447.5 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 204.9 million in the nine months to 2026-06-30, the Board refreshed a USD 400 million authorisation in May 2026, the quarterly dividend was raised to USD 0.33 per share from USD 0.30, and the Term Loan B was increased by USD 325 million on 2026-05-27 while operating cash flow was negative; this is a mixed signal, not extraction, because the buybacks were funded in part by borrowing but leverage stayed within the covenant limits the company reports.

Basis: calculation B4; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_mms-2026x03x31x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4

Ownership and governance evidence is thin. The annual report incorporates director, compensation, ownership and related-party information by reference to a proxy statement that was not supplied, so shareholder concentration, board independence and fees are not established; what is visible is a separate Chair, eight directors including the chief executive, effective internal control over financial reporting, an unqualified audit opinion, and a bar on shareholder action by written consent. None of a sponsor, a controlling holder or a related-party payment is disclosed in the supplied documents.

Legal and operating-risk claims are accrued but unquantified. The class actions that followed the 2023 file-transfer cybersecurity incident continue, about half of the claims against the company remain, and the amount accrued is not stated; performance bond commitments were USD 33.2 million at 2025-09-30.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against concern is that Maximus has no sponsor, a record backlog, margins that rose in fiscal 2026 (adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.0% over nine months against 13.2%), a cash-generative fiscal 2025 and an explanation for the weak cash flow that management says is administrative and already reversing. The same facts also support the opposite reading: scale and margin gains sit on a few cancellable contracts, and the cash shortfall coincided with continued buybacks.

The view improves if collections normalise, with days sales outstanding below 70 days by the year end and free cash flow inside the guidance range of USD 425 million to USD 475 million, and if repurchases slow until they do. It worsens if a top-ten contract is lost or cut, if the customer modification is extended beyond 2026-12-31, if federal payment delays recur, or if buybacks continue to be funded by borrowing while operating cash flow is negative.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Limitations

- The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so ownership concentration, board independence, executive pay and related-party dealings are not established, and the medium governance risk level could move either way when it is read.

- No document reports results after 2026-06-30, so the effect of the customer modification on the second half and whether collections recovered are known only from management's statements, which limits the cash-flow conclusion.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4

- The filings do not name the major customer behind the contract modification and the late payments, so concentration cannot be tied to a named agency or contract beyond the statement that one federal agency supplied about one-fifth of fiscal 2025 revenue.

- No credit agreement was supplied, so the legal capacity behind each capital allocation flag, including baskets for restricted payments and debt, is not established and the behaviour categories describe documented actions only.

## Request

MAXIMUS, INC. (mms), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot: the fundamental credit read of the issuer, built on the financial foundation and business and governance work for the seven supplied SEC filings and earnings releases. The latest period covered is the quarter ended 2026-06-30.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Maximus is an adequate credit: scale, a long contract life and strong interest cover support it, while rising leverage and weak cash conversion from one slow-paying federal customer constrain it, so collections and buybacks, not solvency, are the creditor issues.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation Q1; calculation Q3

Net debt was 2.21x last-twelve-month EBITDA at 2026-06-30 against 1.68x at 2025-09-30, or 1.87x pro forma for the USD 245 million collected after the quarter end (date not stated) and 2.24x pro forma for the dividend payable on 2026-08-31, while cash interest cover was 8.28x. The balance sheet can absorb a delayed receipt, but it depends on that receipt arriving: unrestricted cash was thin and the revolver was the main buffer.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation Q1; calculation Q2; calculation Q3; calculation N5
### Key findings

Debt has grown faster than earnings, and that is the main reason the credit has weakened. Carrying-value debt rose 22.68% from 2025-09-30 to 2026-06-30 while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA rose 7.86%, as the Term Loan B was increased by USD 325 million and buybacks continued; the company's own covenant ratio was 2.00x, on a different definition.
Basis: calculation N1; calculation Q1; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Cash conversion, not profitability, is the weak point. Nine-month operating cash flow was negative because a federal customer delayed payments, days sales outstanding reached 98 days against 62 days at 2025-09-30, and unrestricted cash fell 74.39%; free cash flow guidance of USD 425 million to USD 475 million for the year depends on a large fourth-quarter recovery, of which the USD 245 million already collected is roughly 35.84% to 38.67%.
Basis: calculation N2; calculation N7; calculation N8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Scale and contract life are the strongest support. Backlog was USD 15,327 million with a weighted remaining life of 5.0 years, credit losses on government receivables have not historically been significant, and margins rose in the nine months; but the ten largest contracts gave about 60% of fiscal 2025 revenue and almost all contracts can be cancelled for convenience, so durability is a function of a few customer decisions.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 71; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Liquidity is adequate only because of committed lines. Cash plus the stated revolver access covered the debt principal due within about fifteen months 8.30x, but a full draw of the revolver would lift carrying-value debt to 3.31x last-twelve-month EBITDA, and the receivables purchase facility is a funding dependency outside reported debt.

Basis: calculation N5; calculation N6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Financial policy is mixed: buybacks of USD 447.5 million in fiscal 2025 exceeded free cash flow and USD 204.9 million more was repurchased in the nine months to 2026-06-30 while debt rose, which would turn adverse for creditors if collections do not recover; there is no sponsor and no related-party leakage is disclosed, but the governance evidence is incomplete.
Basis: calculation N3; calculation N4; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The primary downside path is a prolonged federal payment delay or the loss or curtailment of a large contract while buybacks and dividends continue, which would push the business onto the revolver; the large maturities do not begin until 2029, so refinancing risk is distant but the facility terms and any lender response are not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a more positive view is that cash interest cover of 8.28x is high, the debt matures in 2029 and 2031, federal segment margins rose, receivables from government customers have not historically carried significant credit risk, and management says the delayed receivable is already converting. If the fourth-quarter recovery arrives and the USD 245 million collected is followed by the rest of the delayed balance, the nine-month cash shortfall will prove timing, and leverage will return towards the fiscal 2025 level of 1.68x.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 71; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation Q2

The view weakens if days sales outstanding stay above 70 days at the year end, if the temporary customer modification is extended beyond 2026-12-31, if a top-ten contract is lost, or if repurchases continue to be funded by borrowing while operating cash flow is negative. It strengthens if collections normalise and the Board slows repurchases until they do.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Limitations

- No document reports a balance sheet or cash flow after 2026-06-30, so whether the fourth-quarter recovery occurred is not established and the weak cash-conversion conclusion rests on management's statements about collections.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4

- The credit agreement was not supplied, so the liquidity and refinancing conclusions rest on the company's summary of covenants and facility size, and covenant headroom, baskets and the revolver's own maturity are not assessed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33
- No rating, market price or peer set was supplied, so the adequate assessment of the credit is an absolute reading and cannot be positioned against comparable issuers or market access.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
- Revolver availability is stated as about USD 730.0 million without a letter-of-credit amount after 2025-09-30, which could reduce it and weakens the liquidity ratio in the calculations.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strongest supports are scale, contract life and interest cover. Revenue of about USD 5,431 million in fiscal 2025 came from long-dated, government-funded programs, with USD 15,327 million of backlog and a weighted remaining life of 5.0 years, and cash interest cover of 8.28x on the last twelve months leaves room for higher debt costs; both persist unless a top contract is lost.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 50; Financial foundation (CP-1)

A third support is the government payer, whose receivables the company says have not historically carried significant credit losses, and a fourth is maturities that start in 2029, so there is no near-term refinancing wall.

The main weaknesses are cash conversion, leverage direction and concentration. Operating cash flow was negative over nine months and unrestricted cash fell sharply, leverage on carrying-value debt rose from 2.02x to 2.29x in nine months, and about 60% of revenue comes from ten contracts, so one payer or one contract change moves the credit; shareholder returns during this period add a fourth weakness.
Basis: calculation N2; calculation Q1; calculation Q4; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; Financial foundation (CP-1)

| Higher debt | Raises leverage on a larger claim | Analyst Interpretation | Thinner creditor cushion | Net debt to EBITDA rose in nine months |
| Buybacks and dividends | Compete with debt service while cash is thin | Analyst Interpretation | Thinner creditor cushion | Repurchases USD 204.9m in nine months |
| Contract concentration | Ten contracts give about 60% of revenue | Documentary Fact | Earnings volatility | Annual report risk factor |

### Company and ownership

Maximus runs government health, eligibility, clinical-assessment and technology programs, earning 56% of fiscal 2025 revenue from U.S. Federal Services, 32% from U.S. Services and 11% from Outside the U.S., with 55.2% of revenue from federal agencies and 21.2% from state agencies other than New York. Because the customers are governments that fund programs by statute, cash-flow visibility is high and receivables carry little credit risk, but the same customers can modify or cancel contracts, so visibility does not equal protection.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–10; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 80; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Maximus is a listed public company with no sponsor, no disclosed controlling holder and a wholly-owned, guarantor subsidiary structure. Creditors therefore rely on the bank facility and operating cash flow rather than on sponsor support; the Board has authorised USD 400 million of repurchases and raised the dividend, and ownership percentages, director independence and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the governance risk level of medium rests on the annual report alone.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103
### Revenue, cost and cash conversion

Revenue durability is average. Performance-based contracts were 54.4% of fiscal 2025 revenue, so volumes on a few large federal programs drive results; U.S. Federal Services revenue fell 2.5% over nine months to 2026-06-30 and U.S. Services fell 6.4%, partly from disposals, while backlog fell 5.2% in fiscal 2025. Management expects U.S. Services to return to organic growth in the fourth quarter and points to Medicaid and SNAP rule changes, but those are expectations, not contracted revenue.

Basis: calculation N10; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 17; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Margin resilience is average to strong. Labor is about two-thirds of cost of revenue and a large share of expenses is fixed, so a lost contract deleverages quickly, yet segment margins improved: the Federal segment operating margin rose to 17.5% over nine months against 15.3% and the group adjusted EBITDA margin to 14.0% against 13.2%, which management attributes to automation and AI-enabled tools; the modification is guided to bring the Federal margin for the year to 16.5% to 17.0%.

Cash conversion is average in a normal year and weak in the latest nine months. Capital spending is light at 1.16% of fiscal 2025 revenue, down from the technology refresh peak, so EBITDA converts to free cash flow when collections are normal: free cash flow was 0.55x reported EBITDA in fiscal 2025. In the nine months to 2026-06-30 receivables absorbed cash, income taxes paid were USD 81.479 million and the free cash flow was negative.

Basis: calculation N11; calculation Q5; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 65–66; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Competition and policy

Competition is credit-neutral to mildly negative. Competitors named in the annual report are large federal contractors and consultancies, buyer power is high because government customers rebid and can cancel for convenience, supplier power sits in labor, and the government may perform work itself, so pricing power is limited and margin gains come from efficiency, not price. Entry barriers are not quantified in the filings.

Policy is the largest outside influence. The 2025 federal statute adds Medicaid redeterminations every six months and work requirements from 2026-12-31 that states may delay, and ties SNAP funding to error rates from fiscal 2028; interest rates matter because part of the debt floats. These factors can raise demand for eligibility work or delay it, and federal budget or contract changes can cut revenue quickly, so they are credit-material and are carried into the monitoring triggers.
### Financial profile and credit quality

The nine financial-profile dimensions assess as follows. Scale and market position is strong; competitive advantage average, resting on scale and incumbent programs, with no switching-cost or retention data stated; business diversification average, with three segments but concentrated federal and top-contract exposure; cost and capex flexibility average; margin stability average; free cash flow stability weak in the latest nine months; ability to refinance and access capital markets average, with bank debt maturing in 2029 and 2031 and no rating or market data supplied; liquidity position average, thin on cash and reliant on the revolver; financial policy and governance average, with returns to shareholders competing with debt service and the proxy statement not supplied.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15

Credit supports are scale, backlog life, interest cover and distant maturities; constraints are leverage direction, cash conversion and concentration; the trend since fiscal 2025 is negative on leverage and cash conversion and positive on margin; the data missing for a firmer view are post-June results, the credit agreement and the proxy statement.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over twelve to twenty-four months the guided fiscal 2026 outcome is revenue of USD 5.2 billion to USD 5.35 billion toward the lower end, adjusted EBITDA margin of about 13.7% and free cash flow of USD 425 million to USD 475 million, all lowered or held after the customer modification; the modification runs to 2026-12-31 and reduces diluted earnings per share by about USD 0.35 per quarter, roughly USD 18.57 million of net income a quarter on about 53.057 million diluted shares. Tailwinds are the Medicaid and SNAP rule changes, pipeline of USD 50.4 billion and AI-enabled efficiency; headwinds are federal payment timing, lower volumes on large federal contracts, a loss-making international segment guided to break even, and floating-rate debt.
Basis: calculation N9; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 17

Over three to five years the credit depends on whether backlog converts, whether state demand arrives on the legislated schedule, and whether management uses cash for debt reduction or shareholder returns. The Term Loan A matures on 2029-05-30 and the Term Loan B on 2031-05-30, so refinancing capacity will depend on leverage and cash conversion in those years.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_mms-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Qualitative downside scenario

The realistic downside is a federal payment delay that lasts longer than management expects, combined with a curtailed large contract. The first operational break is a receivable build that turns operating cash flow negative again, as it did in the nine months to 2026-06-30; cash, which was USD 56.953 million, is then replenished from the revolver (stated access about USD 730.0 million), from receivable sales (limit USD 350.0 million) or from new debt, and if the revolver were fully drawn carrying-value debt would reach 3.31x last-twelve-month EBITDA, an arithmetic bound that is not a covenant measure. Management's levers are slowing buybacks, trimming the dividend and capital spending, and the revolver; the resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 on the stated facilities, subject to terms of the credit agreement that were not supplied, and the observable triggers are days sales outstanding above 98 days, revolver drawings, a lower guidance range and further repurchases.
Basis: calculation N6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mms-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 31–32; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_mms-2026x06x30x8kxex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Overall credit view

Overall, Maximus presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, contract life and a government customer base, but credit quality is constrained by rising debt, weak recent cash conversion and shareholder returns that continued while cash was thin. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because fiscal 2025 free cash flow was strong and the delayed receipts are being collected, but the recovery is not yet shown in a balance sheet. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage and collections in 2029 and 2031. The primary downside path is a prolonged federal payment delay or a lost large contract while shareholder returns continue. Further analysis would require the results after 2026-06-30, the credit agreement and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: federal collections.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
